BiblicalUsage: Baal-peor was the god of Peor, and the sin at Peor was Israel joining itself to him: the men of Israel yoked themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, Phinehas stopped the plague with his spear, and Moses warned the next generation that their eyes had seen what the Lord did because of Baal-peor. Hosea says they went to Baal-peor and separated themselves to shame.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Peor is the warning that idolatry is never just an idea — it is a yoke, a meal, a shame. And I hold that Phinehas, who stood up and stopped the plague, is the picture of zeal that God honours.
